given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)

breaks.break: treats a loan due today as overdue (<=)
ignores dueOn and reminds every open loan
does not remind a loan that is overdue
computes 'today' from the server's local zone instead of UTC

given.why: The clock is always 10:00Z, so a local-date versus UTC-date mix-up would not fail any test. The boundary cases are only pinned by B2's test.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today

breaks.break: sends again even though a reminder was recorded today
treats a reminder recorded on an earlier day as today's and suppresses the send

given.why: B1 only covers loans with no reminders at all. No test has a reminder from a previous day, so a reminder from any day could block today's send and every test would still pass.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member

breaks.break: sends the wrong member, such as the loanId as memberId
sends for only one of the loans

then.why: Two members and two loans with exact memberId, loanId and dueOn, plus a length check.

then.part: then records a reminder for today

breaks.break: records before asking, so a refusal still leaves a record

then.why: The recording itself is checked here, with a due date distinct from today. The ask-before-record ordering is only proven by B3, which is also what mutants.json says.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today

breaks.break: ignores recorded reminders and sends again
treats a reminder from an earlier day as 'today' and suppresses the send

given.why: The second run proves a same-day reminder suppresses the send. No test has a reminder from another day, so a check that matches any reminder would pass.

breaks.break: does not filter on returned_on and reminds a returned loan

given.why: loan2 is overdue and returned, and the exact-length sent list excludes it.

breaks.break: treats a loan due today as overdue (<=)

given.why: loan3 is due exactly today, which is the boundary case, and it is excluded.

then.why: toMatchObject against a one-element array requires the exact length, so any extra send fails it.

given.why: The fake refuses one specific loan with a reason, and the assertions cover the outcome.

breaks.break: an unreachable API is not turned into a refusal

given.why: The service test only uses the 'refused' result. B5's test proves that a failed connection becomes a refusal.

breaks.break: records the reminder despite the refusal

then.why: The reminders table is compared exactly, so it holds only loan2's row.

then.part: logs `reminder.failed` at `warn` with `loanId` and the refusal's `error`

breaks.break: error is a constant string instead of the refusal's reason
also logs reminder.failed for loans that were accepted

then.why: toContainEqual only requires the entry to exist. A spurious failure log for the accepted loan2 would pass.

then.part: carries on with the other loans

breaks.break: stops at the first refusal (break instead of continue)

then.why: The refused loan1 was lent first and is due earlier, so it is processed first, and loan2 must still be sent.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan

breaks.break: logs the summary before all loans are processed, so the counts are partial
logs the summary more than once, or not as the last entry

given.why: Three overdue loans are handled, one of them refused, and the last log entry is checked.

breaks.break: sent and failed swapped or not counted

then.why: An exact toEqual on the last entry, with the distinct counts 2 and 1.

breaks.break: the client builds the request from the wrong reminder fields

given.why: A concrete reminder is passed straight to the client, and its fields are asserted in the request body.

then.part: Sends `POST {NOTIFY_URL}/notifications` with JSON `{ memberId, template: loan-overdue, data: { loanId, dueOn } }`

breaks.break: memberId key renamed or wrong value
data.loanId or data.dueOn renamed or wrong

then.why: An exact toEqual on the recorded method, path, content-type and parsed body.
Three different 2xx statuses are all accepted.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status

breaks.break: reason is generic and omits the status

then.why: A 400 must be refused and the reason must contain '400'.

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable

breaks.break: the network error propagates instead of becoming a refusal

then.why: HttpResponse.error() simulates a failed connection, and the test expects a refusal whose reason contains 'unreachable'.
